name: Swim: Rotation Block
description: Freestyle technique session built around body rotation. Drills go first while you're fresh, then swim normally with one thing to think about. Distances are in LENGTHS (one way). Roughly 1200-1500 total.

dayOverview.theme: Rotation is the whole session. Tired shoulders and legs that contribute nothing are the same problem — a flat body makes the arms do all the work and leaves the kick disconnected. Everything here is about getting the body to roll.

spotlights.why: The highest-yield drill for a self-taught swimmer who has never drilled. It forces rotation, forces the legs to work, and teaches breathing off the roll — all with the arms parked so they can't compensate.

watchpoints: Water in the mouth on a breath is a LATE roll, not a small one. Arrive on your side before you ask for air, and keep the lower goggle wet.
🛑 Nothing here is an effort session. If you're breathing hard on the drills, they're being swum instead of drilled — slow down.
🛑 Right shoulder: freestyle recovery is a big overhead arc. If it gets crabby, stop the swim, not just the drill.
Count strokes on one length near the start and one near the end. That's the only number worth having, and it should drift DOWN over weeks.

exercises.notes: Easy. No thinking, no fixing. Just get wet and let the shoulders open up.

🔆 **The session.** **Two lengths on your LEFT side for every one on your right.**
- The left-side position — **left arm extended forward**, right shoulder pointing at the sky — is the one that trains right-side breathing. That's the side still catching up, so it gets the extra length.
- **Bottom arm straight forward**, top arm resting along the hip — arms are parked, not helping.
- **Eyes straight down** at the bottom of the pool. Lower goggle under, upper goggle out. Neck neutral — don't jam the chin, just don't look forward.
- **Small fast kick from the HIPS**, not the knees. On your side there's nowhere to hide: no kick, no movement.
- **To breathe, roll back toward your spine** until the face clears. Roll, don't crane the neck. Then roll back down.
- **Keep the lower goggle in the water the whole time.** Your head drags a bow wave and there's a trough beside it — your mouth breathes in that trough, below the flat surface. Lift for air and you leave the trough and get the wave instead.
- **What holds you up is your chest, not your arms.** Your lungs are the float and they sit high; your legs are dense and sit low. **Lean on your sternum** — press the chest a few degrees toward the bottom and the body seesaws over the lungs, and the legs rise. This is the whole trick.
- **The extended bottom arm is a balance lever, not a paddle.** Reach it long and slightly DOWN, not up toward the surface. Length forward is what stops the legs dropping.
- **Point the toes.** A flexed foot is a brake — it stops the kick lifting anything.
- **If you're still sinking, cut the distance.** Half a length in good position, stand up, reset. A wobbling full length grooves the wobble.

Same side position as above, now connected: **6 kicks on one side → 3 strokes → 6 kicks on the other side.** The 3 strokes are just the bridge between two side-kick positions. Stay long, let the hips lead the shoulders.
- **Breathe during the 6 kicks, not during the 3 strokes.** You are already fully on your side there, so the breath costs nothing extra. That's the feeling to steal for real swimming.

exercises.distance: as far as feels good — around 40 lengths
exercises.notes:
Normal swimming. **One thought only: roll on EVERY stroke, not just the breathing ones.**
- If you arrive at the breath already on your side, the breath is nearly free — the face is almost clear before you ask for air.
- **Lead arm stays long and patient.** On a right-side breath that's the LEFT arm out front. If it presses down early the shoulder drops and the mouth goes under.
- Keep alternating sides — left, right, left. The right side gets easier as the roll improves, not by forcing it.
- **Count strokes on one length** early and one late. Same effort, fewer strokes = it's working.
- Stop when it stops feeling good. The distance is not the point.
Easy backstroke — opens the chest and unloads the front of the shoulder after all that freestyle.

tips: Drills go FIRST, while you're fresh. A drill done tired just grooves the bad version.
Slow is correct on the drills. They are not conditioning.
If the throat gums up partway through, ease off for a length and clear it rather than pushing through — outdoor pools and a steady nose-exhale both help.
Breathing on both sides is the right pattern. The weak side is a rotation problem, not a weak-side problem.
Stroke count is the only number worth tracking here. Not laps, not time.
